body:
No, this, won't work. The whole point of this code is to clear the navigation data if it gets disabled. (so if it goes from `true` to `false`). So this definitely wrong. 
You can check where `forced_cleanup` is set:
```
bool forced_cleanup = p_force_cleanup || !enabled || !navigation_enabled || !is_inside_tree() || tile_set.is_null();
```
This added condition means this code is never executed (which, indeed, could speed up performance).

Now, this full cleanup shouldn't be done often. Only when you toggle navigation or you modify the TileSet. `set_cell` shouldn't never cause a full cleanup. If it does, then that's the cause of the issue.

I think there's some confusion about the naming. `DIRTY_FLAGS_LAYER_NAVIGATION_ENABLED` isn't just set to true when navigation is enabled, it's set when `navigation_enabled` is updated *at all*. [You can see that here.](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/7924993359a178f9c8670aaeeb2d40dd840779c0/scene/2d/tile_map_layer.cpp#L3405) I went ahead and tested this out by adding a `print_line` inside of this block, and it prints just fine when the state is toggled off. This absolutely does still run the cleanup once, as it should. The performance gain is real. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cdb6f851-6782-401b-a4b5-a5f29899b4b2 Here's a log from a game instead of the editor showcasing the same thing: > Now, this full cleanup shouldn't be done often. Only when you toggle navigation or you modify the TileSet. set_cell shouldn't never cause a full cleanup. If it does, then that's the cause of the issue. That is indeed both what is happening in the issue and the fix I believe I have implemented in this PR.

> I think there's some confusion about the naming. DIRTY_FLAGS_LAYER_NAVIGATION_ENABLED isn't just set to true when navigation is enabled, it's set when navigation_enabled is updated at all. You can see that here.

Yeah, and that should be fine. There should be no issue in the navigation being cleared as there's nothing to clear. But in any case the logic isn't right anyway.

The `forced_cleanup` variable should be the only bool involved there. It's the bool defining whether or not things should be cleaned up or not. If there's an issue in how this bool is computed, please change it's value in the upper line and don't add another condition here.

If we really need that perf increase, then the logic should likely to early exit the function if both `forced_cleanup` and `_navigation_was_cleaned_up` are true (that should avoid double-cleanups). 

But in any case, I'd rather see the performance changes that implies. The `_navigation_clear_cell` should do nothing if navigation data was already cleared (since the `cell_data.navigation_regions` array should be empty).

I agree that it makes more sense to fix in `forced_cleanup`. I realized basically the same issue occurs if the other parts of the condition are met, so I updated the entire condition. I needed to add a condition on the lower block because it relied on the cleanup being run every time.

Even if `_navigation_clear_cell` ends up doing no work, doing it the sheer number of times that does still ends up being the majority of the time on the flamegraph in the linked issue, so avoiding it is important.

I think what you pushed there is still more complex than just exiting the function if `_navigation_was_cleaned_up == forced_cleanup`. It should cover most cases while avoiding potential issues.

And while doing so you can:
- Implement the same logic for all subsystems (see where other `*_was_cleaned_up` variables are used in other functions)
- Initialize all `*_was_cleaned_up` variables to `true` instead of false (that should avoid iterating over all cells at startup).
